content: 1. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate reduces the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (trivalent, intranasal) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Its use is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also elevate the risk of infection when administered alongside live vaccines. 2. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate diminishes the effects of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants further increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 3. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or consider alternative medications. 4. Isoflurane and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and leflunomide both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Immunosuppressive therapies (e.g., radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, corticosteroids at doses exceeding physiologic levels) may reduce the immune response to the dengue vaccine. 102. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and denosumab require caution in patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems due to an increased risk of serious infections. Use caution and monitor closely. 103. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances may increase the risk of torsades de pointes.
